title: Health Ministry Proposes Good Distribution Practice Rules for Drug Licensees

contentHtml:
New Delhi: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed making compliance with Good Distribution Practices Guidelines a condition for licence holders under nine provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945.

The proposal is contained in draft notification G.S.R. 984(E), dated November 4, 2026, and published in the Gazette dated November 12, 2026. The requirements would take effect only if the rules are finalised.

The draft seeks to add a definition of “Guidelines on Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP) for Pharmaceutical Products” to Rule 2. It describes these as guidelines formulated by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation and adopted by the Drugs Technical Advisory Board to ensure the quality and identity of pharmaceutical products throughout distribution in India.

The proposed compliance condition would be inserted into Rules 26, 33A, 65, 74, 74A, 74B, 78, 78A and 122P. In each case, the draft uses the same requirement:

"The licensee shall ensure compliance with the Good Distribution Practices Guidelines."

The notification does not set a fixed commencement date. It says the Government would specify that date when the rules are finally published in the Official Gazette. The draft was issued after consultation with the Drugs Technical Advisory Board under Sections 12(1) and 33(1) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

The Central Government will consider objections and suggestions received within 30 days from the date copies of the Gazette containing the draft are made available to the public. Submissions may be sent to the Under Secretary (Drugs), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhavan 1, New Delhi–110001, or emailed to drugsdiv-mohfw@gov.in.
